title: Flat extension identifies extended localization Čech complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ global sections of $\mathcal O$, with $r\geq0$. Assume $\mathcal B$ is flat over $\mathcal O$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $\mathcal O/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\mathcal O\to\mathcal B/(\varphi(f_1),\ldots,\varphi(f_r))\mathcal B$ is an isomorphism of ring sheaves. $C(\mathcal O;f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ denotes the extended alternating localization complex: its degree zero is $\mathcal O$, its degree $q$ for $1\leq q\leq r$ is $\prod_{i_1<\cdots<i_q}\mathcal O[1/(f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_q})]$, and all other terms are zero. The differential is the alternating sum of localization maps, and its augmentation to $\mathcal O[0]$ is the identity in degree zero and zero in other degrees. For $r=0$ it is $\mathcal O[0]$. Define $C(\mathcal B;\varphi(f_1),\ldots,\varphi(f_r))$ by the same formula. The map induced termwise by $\varphi$, $$C(\mathcal O;f_1,\ldots,f_r)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}C(\mathcal B;\varphi(f_1),\ldots,\varphi(f_r)),$$ is a quasi-isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Here module sheaves and restriction of scalars are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

proof.text: For r=0, the ideal rows have zero source, so their cokernel projections are isomorphisms. The cokernel comparison equation and the quotient hypothesis imply unitMap phi is an isomorphism. Restriction of scalars preserves coproducts, so comparisonTerm is the coproduct of that isomorphism followed by the coproduct comparison isomorphism. Thus every comparisonStage is an isomorphism.

For r>0, use the signed Koszul contraction theorem to show that the uniform positive power r*(n+1)+1 of the ideal generated by the f_j(X) annihilates every section of every stage cohomology sheaf, on every object X. In degrees 0<=q<=r, apply the flat torsion tensor comparison to obtain the invertible tensor unit map on cohomology and the finite free complex comparison isomorphism. Flatness supplies preservation of finite limits and colimits for the tensor functor. Naturality of the exact-functor homology isomorphisms shows that the complex map of the tensor unit transformation induces an isomorphism on homology: cancel the two canonical homology isomorphisms from NatTrans.app_homology. Factoring comparisonStage through this map and the two complex isomorphisms proves invertibility of its homology map. Outside the stated degree range the index type is empty, since the cardinality of a subset of Fin r lies between 0 and r; hence both terms and both homology objects are zero. This proves every stage comparison is a quasi-isomorphism.

Pointwise multiplication and the ring morphism law show scalar(f_j) followed by unitMap equals unitMap followed by the restricted target scalar. Induction on the ordered subset product gives the same identity for transition coefficients. Coproduct extensionality then proves that the stage comparisons form a natural transformation of the sequential Koszul diagrams.

The exact faithful forgetful functor to abelian sheaves preserves colimits. Restriction of scalars commutes with that forgetful functor, which reflects colimits, so restriction preserves colimits as well. Exact filtered colimits of abelian sheaves transfer to module sheaves through this forgetful functor. Apply the proved generic theorem HomologicalComplex.isStableUnderColimitsOfShape_quasiIso to the natural transformation of stages, with the source colimit cocone and the preserved target colimit cocone. Its induced map is exactly comparison by colimit.ι_desc, yielding the desired quasi-isomorphism.
